candidates.source_name: Sindikat bančništva Slovenije (SBS)
candidates.why_relevant: Representative sector trade union for banking in Slovenia (founded 1990, representative since 1993); signatory/negotiator of the Kolektivna pogodba dejavnosti bančništva Slovenije. Site lists constituent member unions at Deželna banka, Gorenjska banka, Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, OTP and SID banka, and hosts statutes, legal-aid rules and collective-agreement documents. Primary channel for the downside of org change (branch closures, post-merger redundancies) and for pay/collective-bargaining disputes.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML crawl of Sindikat / Dokumenti / member-union pages; no obvious RSS observed, so diff-based polling of document listings plus PDF harvesting.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on union name + collective agreement terms, then direct fetch of homepage
queries_used: Sindikat bančništva Slovenije kolektivna pogodba pogajanja
zapiranje poslovalnic banke Slovenija presežni delavci sindikat

candidates.source_name: Sindikat finančnih organizacij Slovenije (SFOS) — ZSSS affiliate
candidates.why_relevant: The second representative union covering 'finančno posredništvo' (financial intermediation), affiliated to ZSSS, seat Dalmatinova 4, Ljubljana. Complements SBS: where SBS covers bank-level units, SFOS extends to insurance/leasing/other financial organisations. Its positions surface in sector bargaining and restructuring disputes.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the SFOS page and the parent ZSSS news feed for statements naming banks/financial organisations.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from ZSSS confederation search
queries_used: ZSSS Zveza svobodnih sindikatov Slovenije bančništvo finančne dejavnosti sindikat

candidates.source_name: Zveza svobodnih sindikatov Slovenije (ZSSS) — confederation site
candidates.why_relevant: Largest Slovenian union confederation, ~22 sector unions. Acts as a pointer/aggregator: publishes confederal statements, tripartite (Ekonomsko-socialni svet) positions, and links to each sector affiliate including SFOS. Useful to snowball actor map and to catch bank restructuring framed as a national labour issue.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl news/announcement listings; keyword-filter for banka, bančn*, finančn*, zavarovaln*.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on confederation name
queries_used: ZSSS Zveza svobodnih sindikatov Slovenije bančništvo finančne dejavnosti sindikat

candidates.source_name: Sindikat Nove Ljubljanske banke (Sindikat NLB)
candidates.why_relevant: House union at Slovenia's largest bank and a distinct bargaining actor: reporting indicates Sindikat NLB signed the 2026 tarifna priloga to the banking collective agreement while SBS refused. Tracking it separates employer-aligned from confrontational union positions and reveals NLB-internal staffing/branch decisions. No confirmed own website found — registry entry used as the anchor record.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Registry entry for entity identification; monitor named mentions in media and Uradni list signature blocks rather than a dedicated site.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on tarifna priloga signature dispute
queries_used: Sindikat NLB tarifna priloga podpis plače banka sindikat 2026

candidates.source_name: Kolektivna pogodba dejavnosti bančništva Slovenije (PISRS register entry)
candidates.why_relevant: The authoritative consolidated text and amendment history of the banking-sector collective agreement on the state legal-information portal. Every renegotiation, tariff annex and change to redundancy/severance rules lands here, giving a dated, citable trail of bargaining outcomes.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Watch the predpis page for new amendment rows; pair with Uradni list issue links for full texts.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on collective agreement name
queries_used: Sindikat bančništva Slovenije kolektivna pogodba pogajanja

candidates.source_name: Uradni list RS — collective agreements and tariff annexes (banking)
candidates.why_relevant: Official gazette where sector collective agreements and their tarifne priloge must be published together with the registration certificate (per ZKolP). Confirmed banking items: the 2024 tariff annex and the 2025 Kolektivna pogodba Banke Slovenije (central bank staff). Gives exact effective dates and signatory lists — the hard evidence behind union press claims.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword-scheduled search of gazette contents for 'kolektivna pogodba' + 'bančništv*' / 'Banke Slovenije'; archive PDFs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from PISRS and collective-agreement register searches
queries_used: evidenca kolektivnih pogodb Ministrstvo za delo register kolektivnih pogodb bančništvo
Sindikat bančništva Slovenije kolektivna pogodba pogajanja

candidates.source_name: Evidenca kolektivnih pogodb (MDDSZ register) via OPSI open-data portal
candidates.why_relevant: Machine-readable register of all collective agreements maintained by the labour ministry (MDDSZ) under Art. 25 ZKolP, published as an open dataset. Lets you enumerate every banking/finance agreement, its parties and its status without scraping — the structural backbone of the bargaining actor map.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled download of the dataset resource; diff against previous snapshot to detect new/terminated agreements.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on the ministry register term
queries_used: evidenca kolektivnih pogodb Ministrstvo za delo register kolektivnih pogodb bančništvo

candidates.source_name: Zavod RS za zaposlovanje (ZRSZ/ESS) — Trg dela v številkah
candidates.why_relevant: The public employment service publishes registered unemployment and reported job vacancies (sporočena prosta delovna mesta) by activity sector, 2005–2026. Because employers must notify ZRSZ 30 days before collective dismissals (ZDR-1 art. 98–99), sector-level inflows are the earliest quantitative echo of bank redundancies. Caveat: SKD 2025 replaced SKD 2008 from 1 Jan 2025, so series break — data are explicitly not comparable across that boundary.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly harvest of the registered-unemployment and vacancy tables filtered to SKD sector K; store SKD version with each series.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on labour-market statistics terms
queries_used: ESS Zavod RS za zaposlovanje statistični podatki trg dela registrirana brezposelnost po dejavnosti odprta delovna mesta

candidates.source_name: ZRSZ Napovednik zaposlovanja (employment forecast survey)
candidates.why_relevant: Semi-annual employer survey in which firms state expected hiring and headcount reduction by activity; gives forward-looking signal on financial-sector staffing intentions ahead of any formal redundancy notice. Published as PDF reports with a stable naming pattern.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the Napovednik zaposlovanja directory twice yearly; extract the K-sector table from the PDF.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from ZRSZ labour-market section
queries_used: ESS Zavod RS za zaposlovanje statistični podatki trg dela registrirana brezposelnost po dejavnosti odprta delovna mesta

candidates.source_name: ZRSZ — Delavci v odpovednem roku (workers under notice) service page
candidates.why_relevant: Describes the employer obligation to notify ZRSZ of collective dismissals and the support programme for workers under notice. Documents the exact procedural trigger and timing (30 days ahead) that makes ZRSZ the earliest official touchpoint for a bank restructuring — essential for designing the collection cadence, and a candidate for FOI/statistical requests.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Reference page; use as basis for an information-access request for aggregate collective-dismissal notifications in SKD K.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on the collective-dismissal notification duty
queries_used: Zavod za zaposlovanje obvestilo o odpuščanju večjega števila delavcev program razreševanja presežkov

candidates.source_name: ZDR-1 art. 99 — Program razreševanja presežnih delavcev (statute text)
candidates.why_relevant: Defines the numeric thresholds (10 workers if 20–100 employed; one tenth if 100–300; >30 if over 300) that force an employer into a formal redundancy programme with union consultation and ZRSZ notification. These thresholds tell you exactly when a bank restructuring becomes publicly detectable versus when it can stay silent — a scoping rule for the whole cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off reference capture; prefer the PISRS canonical ZDR-1 text for citation.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on redundancy-programme term
queries_used: Zavod za zaposlovanje obvestilo o odpuščanju večjega števila delavcev program razreševanja presežkov

candidates.source_name: SiStat / SURS — employment in financial and insurance activities (SKD K)
candidates.why_relevant: National statistical office database with employed/self-employed persons, labour costs and structural business statistics broken down by activity and size class; sector K (financial and insurance activities) is covered as a complete field. Provides the authoritative denominator for any headcount claim about Slovenian banking and a long back-series for trend work.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: PxWeb API queries against employment and structural-business tables filtered to SKD K; scheduled refresh on SURS release calendar.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on SURS sector-K employment statistics
queries_used: SURS SiStat zaposlene osebe finančne in zavarovalniške dejavnosti K statistika

candidates.source_name: SURS StatWeb — news releases and methodological notes (plače, podjetja)
candidates.why_relevant: SURS first-release notes and methodological explanations (structural wage statistics, wages, enterprise demography) carry the narrative and definitions behind the SiStat tables, including for financial activities. Needed to interpret breaks such as the SKD 2008 to SKD 2025 change and to date releases correctly.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Subscribe to / poll the StatWeb news index; keyword filter on plače, zaposleni, finančne dejavnosti.
candidates.discovered_via_method: snowballed from SiStat search results
queries_used: SURS SiStat zaposlene osebe finančne in zavarovalniške dejavnosti K statistika

candidates.source_name: ZSDS — Združenje svetov delavcev Slovenije / ŠCID (works councils association)
candidates.why_relevant: The national association of works councils (svet delavcev), over 110 member councils, run through the Študijski center za industrijsko demokracijo in Kranj. Works councils hold statutory co-determination and information/consultation rights over status changes, mergers and headcount decisions — the second workforce channel besides unions. The site publishes recommendations, case articles and the Ekonomska demokracija material via its strokovniclanki subdomain.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the main site plus strokovniclanki.delavska-participacija.com article archive; keyword-filter for banka/bančn*/zavarovaln*; harvest PDFs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on works councils / worker participation
queries_used: svet delavcev banka Slovenija delavska participacija ZSDS združenje svetov delavcev

candidates.why_relevant: EU-level database of large-scale restructuring events, updated from national media, with roughly 487 Slovenian cases recorded and searchable by sector, type and date; includes historical banking cases (e.g. an NKBM job-cut case). negative_findings.description: The SBS homepage was fetched directly. Its navigation is limited to Sindikat, Članstvo, Zaposleni, Kontakt and Dokumenti; no 'Novice' section and no RSS feed were visible on the page.
negative_findings.result_summary: The single most important union in this cell has no observable news channel, so its positions reach the public mainly through media (Delo, Megafon) rather than through its own site.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design cannot rely on an SBS feed; it must combine document-listing diffing with media keyword monitoring, otherwise union statements will be missed entirely.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovenian for Sindikat NLB. Only a business-registry entry and media mentions were returned; no own website or press page was found in the results reviewed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Company-level bank unions in Slovenia appear largely to lack independent web presence.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: House unions are decisive actors (Sindikat NLB signed the 2026 tariff annex that SBS rejected) yet are only observable second-hand, which weakens attribution and timing precision.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovenian for the employer duty to notify ZRSZ of collective dismissals. The obligation and its 30-day deadline are well documented, but no public register or dataset of individual notifications was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: The earliest official signal of a bank restructuring exists as an administrative filing that is not published.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The highest-value leading indicator in this cell is not directly collectable; it must be approached via aggregate ZRSZ statistics or an information-access request, which introduces lag.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovenian combining works councils with banks. ZSDS/ŠCID was identified as the association, but no bank-specific works-council material surfaced in the results reviewed.
negative_findings.result_summary: Works councils exist as an institution with a national association, but bank-level council activity is not visible on the open web.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Works councils have statutory information/consultation rights over mergers and headcount decisions, so their invisibility removes a channel that should in principle pre-date public announcements.

negative_findings.description: English-language search for 2026 Slovenian bank branch closures and union statements returned only older material (a 2020 programme of roughly 300 job cuts, a Slovak factoring unit closure of 307 jobs) and general group pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: English-only searching does not reach current Slovenian workforce news; the Slovenian-language searches returned materially different and more current results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms empirically that this cell cannot be run in English; monolingual English collection would have produced a false picture of quiescence.

negative_findings.description: Searched UNI Europa for the Slovenian affiliate by its acronym SBS. The federation's material on CEE bargaining (BARSERVICE project) was found, but no page naming a Slovenian banking affiliate appeared in the results reviewed.
negative_findings.result_summary: The Slovenian banking union's European affiliation could not be confirmed from the results obtained; 'SBS' is also a noisy acronym.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without confirmed affiliation, the European federation cannot be relied on as a proxy feed for Slovenian union positions.

coverage_gaps.description: Company-level bank unions beyond NLB — at OTP banka (post-merger, covering former Nova KBM and SKB units), Addiko, Delavska hranilnica, Sberbank/N Banka successor entities, Banka Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit and Gorenjska banka — were not individually located, although SBS lists several as member unions.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate SBS member unions from its own site and resolve each in AJPES; then monitor their names as media keywords and as signatories in Uradni list collective-agreement texts.

coverage_gaps.description: Two workforce-side institutions were identified conceptually but not yet located as concrete sources: the Ekonomsko-socialni svet (tripartite social and economic council, where sector disputes escalate) and the Inšpektorat RS za delo (IRSD), whose annual reports aggregate labour-law violations by activity.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run dedicated Slovenian searches for 'Ekonomsko-socialni svet seje dnevni red' and 'Inšpektorat RS za delo letno poročilo dejavnost K' and add the resulting gov.si pages as sources.

coverage_gaps.description: ZRSZ and SURS both publish at SKD sector level (K = financial and insurance activities), which merges banking with insurance and other finance. No banking-only (K64) monthly employment series was located, and the SKD 2008 to SKD 2025 changeover on 1 January 2025 breaks comparability.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test whether the SiStat PxWeb API exposes two-digit K64 breakdowns; if not, document the sector-level constraint and record the SKD version alongside every stored observation.

coverage_gaps.description: The topic 'leadership moves' is only weakly served by this cell. Union and labour-market sources cover rank-and-file headcount, not management appointments; management-board changes are disclosed through supervisory-board and regulatory channels outside this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Rely on the issuer-disclosure and regulator cells for management-board changes; from this cell, contribute only union-leadership changes and union reactions to management appointments.

coverage_gaps.description: The cell rationale flags outsourcing as a harm channel, but no Slovenian source specific to bank IT/back-office outsourcing or shared-service-centre transfers of staff was found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add targeted Slovenian queries such as 'banka zunanje izvajanje storitev prenos zaposlenih' and 'skupni storitveni center banka Slovenija zaposleni' in a follow-up pass.

coverage_gaps.description: Most candidates were identified through search-result metadata; only the SBS homepage was fetched directly. Liveness, feed availability and robots/ToS constraints are therefore unconfirmed for the remainder.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Let the deterministic verification pass check reachability and robots.txt for every URL; treat any single failure as bot-defence rather than as a dead source.

brief: Slovenia's workforce-side banking intelligence rests on a narrow but high-quality set of actors: Sindikat bančništva Slovenije (representative since 1993, negotiator of the Kolektivna pogodba dejavnosti bančništva) plus the ZSSS-affiliated SFOS, with company-level house unions such as Sindikat NLB acting as separate and sometimes opposing signatories — the 2026 tarifna priloga was signed by Sindikat NLB but rejected by SBS over inflation indexation. The paradox of the cell is that these unions publish almost nothing themselves: SBS has no news feed or RSS, and house unions have no websites, so their positions become observable only through Delo, Večer, Megafon, RTV SLO and 24ur's 'zapiranje poslovalnic' tag, while the authoritative texts land in Uradni list, PISRS and the MDDSZ collective-agreement register (available as an OPSI open dataset). Quantitatively the cell is anchored by SURS SiStat and ZRSZ 'Trg dela v številkah', both only at SKD sector K granularity and both broken by the SKD 2008 to SKD 2025 changeover; the strongest leading indicator — the employer's mandatory 30-day collective-dismissal notification to ZRSZ — exists but is not published, making Eurofound's ERM Slovenia database and the ZBS branch-hours directory the best practical early-warning proxies. Local-language searching was decisive: identical English queries returned only 2020-era restructuring material, while Slovenian queries surfaced current bargaining and the OTP/Nova KBM/SKB integration staffing story.
